newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Japan's emperor gets big welcome in Sao Paulo.
newsitem.headline: Japan's emperor gets big welcome in Sao Paulo.

text.p: Japanese Emperor Akihito and Empress Michiko, midway through a 10-day day visit to Brazil, were greeted Thursday with shouts of "Banzai" from thousands of Sao Paulo's Japanese community, the largest outside Japan.
Making the first Japanese imperial visit to Latin America, the emperor and empress smiled broadly and waved to some 8,000 Japanese-Brazilians who packed into a gymnasium to get a glimpse of them.
In a brief message, Akihito praised the courage and determination of Japanese immigrants who began arriving in Brazil 90 years ago to farm its vast interior.
"Thank you Brazil, for accepting our people so warmly," Akihito said.
The crowd waved Japanese and Brazilian flags and chanted Japan's national patriotic cry "Banzai."
As Akihito entered the gymnasium, he was stopped by an elderly farmer who said it was the first Thursday he had taken off work in his life. "I did this to see you," the farmer said.
Sao Paulo, Brazil's sprawling industrial capital, is home to most of the 1.3 million Brazilians of Japanese descent.

While most of the early Japanese immigrants cleared forests for coffee cultivation in the interior of Sao Paulo, many later migrated to the city where they opened small businesses or started professional practices.
Today, after decades of booming economic growth in Japan, thousands of Japanese-Brazilians have opted to return to their ancestral home to improve their quality of life.

Some 170,000 'dekassegui,' or Japanese Brazilians working in Japan, sent home $4 billion in 1995. The flows are so steady that federal bank Banco do Brasil used the remittances to back a bond issue last year.
The dekassegui, who now number 200,000, have complained they are treated as second-class citizens in Japan. But Akihito said his nation valued the contribution they have made to Japan.
Brazil and Japan are key trading partners, with some $6.5 billion in goods traded in 1995. Japan also provides Brazil with technical and financial aid.
The imperial couple lunched with Sao Paulo state Gov. Mario Covas, and were expected to visit a mausoleum of early Japanese immigrants and a museum of Japanese history in Brazil.
They were also due to tour the Japanese neighbourhood of Liberdade. Akihito and Michiko are in Brazil until Monday, when they fly to Buenos Aires for a three-day visit to Argentina.
